# Skeleton change
- CHANGE `esper/__init__.py::World.create_entity(self, *components: _C) -> int` — always registers the new entity in `_entities` (as empty if no components are given), then attaches any components
- CHANGE `esper/__init__.py::World.add_component(self, entity: int, component_instance: _C, type_alias: _Optional[_Type[_C]] = None) -> None` — adds a component to an existing entity only; raises KeyError if the entity was never created, and no longer creates entities
- CHANGE `esper/__init__.py::World.remove_component(self, entity: int, component_type: _Type[_C]) -> int` — removes the component but keeps the entity registered even when it has no components left
- CHANGE `esper/__init__.py::World.entity_exists(self, entity: int) -> bool` — True for any created, not-deleted entity, including empty ones
- RULE `esper/__init__.py::World.add_component` may not create entries in `World._entities` — only `World.create_entity` registers entities (single responsibility)

I wrote the skeleton change to `SKELETON.md`. It has four CHANGE lines and one RULE line, all in `esper/__init__.py`:

- **`World.create_entity`** always registers the new entity, even when no components are given. This is the fix the report proposes.
- **`World.add_component`** only works on an entity that already exists and raises `KeyError` otherwise. It no longer creates entities.
- **`World.remove_component`** keeps the entity registered after its last component is removed. This one isn't in the report: right now, removing the last component deletes the entity. Without this line, an entity could still disappear while it is empty.
- **`World.entity_exists`** returns True for empty entities too. Its docstring currently says empty entities don't count, so that wording has to change.
- **RULE:** only `World.create_entity` may add entities to `World._entities`; `World.add_component` may not. This follows from the report's single-responsibility point.
